newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD, DORTMUND COME UNSTUCK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD, DORTMUND COME UNSTUCK.

text.p: Bayern Munich opened up a big lead at the top of the German first division with a 3-2 win over Cologne on Saturday while challengers Borussia Dortmund lost 3-2 at lowly Duisburg.
Two goals from Italian striker Ruggiero Rizzitelli and one from Juergen Klinsmann earned the Bavarians a home victory and put them five points clear on 58 points with seven matches left to play.
Meanwhile European Cup semifinalists Dortmund, bidding for a third straight title, fell to fourth place with a surprise defeat away to their local rivals.
VfB Stuttgart moved above them into third place with a 5-1 demolition of struggling Hansa Rostock featuring goals from their "magic triangle" of Krasimir Balakov, Giovane Elber and Fredi Bobic.
Bayern's nearest rivals after the weekend fixtures, Bayer Leverkusen, kept their title hopes alive with a 3-1 home victory over Karlsruhe on Friday.
Leverkusen now have 53 points and Stuttgart and Dortmund both have 52.
